text:
Leah H.: heads-up — we need to shift the eu-west Dedicated maintenance window by 2 hours. original window clashed with a customer data migration. want to propose new window: 02:00–04:00 UTC on 2027-06-15. low-risk rolling restarts but could cause short evictions (1–3 min) on some nodes.

Ashwin R.: ok — do we expect any SLA blips or perf degradation for Hosted customers?

Leah H.: hosted unaffected. Dedicated only; customers on reserved pools might see a few token delays while nodes rotate. fallback routing should keep requests alive. SLA hit unlikely but we should notify customers proactively.

Jon B.: +1 on proactive. we should prepare: status page message, email template for affected tenants, and an internal incident handoff note. I can take on-call for the window if needed.

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance job created: maintenance-id 20270615-euw-rot. start=2027-06-15T02:00:00Z, end=2027-06-15T04:00:00Z. Notify channels: #announcements, #eng-oncall, #support.

Katie (Support): can we get a short customer-facing blurb? support needs to triage any emails.

Leah H.: draft below — please edit.

Leah H.: STATUS PAGE DRAFT (please copy for account emails):

```
Title: Scheduled maintenance — eu-west dedicated capacity (2027-06-15)
Impact: Some customers using Dedicated (reserved) capacity in eu-west may experience brief interruptions (under 3 minutes) for requests served from affected nodes. Hosted API customers are not impacted.
Start: 2027-06-15 02:00 UTC
End: 2027-06-15 04:00 UTC
What we're doing: rolling infrastructure upgrades to improve stability and scheduling performance.
What you can expect: brief reconnects / slightly elevated latency for specific requests during node rotation. No data loss expected. Our routing will automatically retry where applicable.
Contact: support@redwood-inference.example
```

Ashwin R.: looks good. add a "who to contact if you have an SLA commitment" line and a short note for customers with pinned model versions that they may want to pause big batch jobs before the window.

Leah H.: updated draft with SLA contact and batch-job note.

Jon B.: oncall handoff plan: I will be primary during the window. Ashwin, can you be backup 02:30–03:30?

Ashwin R.: yes I can take backup 02:30–03:30.

Leah H.: @incident-bot, please schedule a 15m pre-window reminder to #eng-oncall and page Jon.

incident-bot: reminder scheduled. will send reminder at 2027-06-15T01:45:00Z and page Jon B..

Leah H.: also tagging #support to prepare canned replies. Katie, i'll paste a trimmed email template after.

Katie (Support): thanks — will prep canned reply and include the SLA escalation contact + link to status page.

Leah H.: CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE (short):

```
Subject: Scheduled maintenance in eu-west (2027-06-15)
Hi <CustomerName>,
We're performing a scheduled maintenance on Dedicated capacity in eu-west on 2027-06-15 from 02:00–04:00 UTC. During this window, you may see brief interruptions (under 3 minutes) for requests routed through affected nodes. No data loss is expected. If you have scheduled large batch jobs, we recommend pausing them until after 04:00 UTC.
If you are on an SLA contract and need assistance, please reply/cc support@redwood-inference.example.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Ops
```

Jon B.: good. also adding an internal checklist for the window:
- confirm canaries 01:50
- verify autoscaler limits before 01:55
- enable extra logging for model-serving during rotate
- be ready to roll back config if cpu/KV-cache evictions spike

SRE Rotation: copied checklist into runbook hub.

-- Maintenance begins --

incident-bot: paging on-call — increased error rate observed for model-serving on pool euw-dedicated-3. trigger: 5xx spike (03:12 UTC). severity: low.

Jon B.: picking this up. looking at logs. initial cause looks like a transient KV-cache refill after node reboot.

Ashwin R.: quick mitigation: bump replica count for pool euw-dedicated-3 and enable short-term hot-cache warmup (run prefetch job). I can run the scaling now.

Jon B.: scaling up by +2 now. also disabled aggressive preemption rule for that node group.

Jon B.: error rate falling. rolling restarts continuing. will monitor for 15m.

incident-bot: incident update: error rate returning to baseline. customers may have seen retries.

Leah H.: posting status page update: maintenance in progress — brief spike observed at 03:12 UTC, mitigated. no further action required for most customers.

Katie (Support): sent proactive emails to affected tenants (list attached). one mid-tier customer replied asking for SLA note — escalated to Account Ops.

Jon B.: handoff notes: Ashwin took backup, scaled pool, we saw a brief 5xx spike during a node rotate, mitigated via scale + warmup, no data loss. monitoring hooks reinstated.

Leah H.: maintenance completed 03:48 UTC — marking as complete. final status page message: completed — rolling upgrades finished, short transient errors mitigated.

incident-bot: maintenance job 20270615-euw-rot marked complete by Leah H. duration 1h48m.

Leah H.: postmortem/action items (quick):
- update runbook to include hot-cache warmup step before rotating any pool (assigned Ashwin)
- add canary ramping 20 minutes earlier (assigned Jon)
- support to include SLA-commit customer call list in future notices (assigned Katie)
- update status page template with explicit 'expected retry behavior' line (assigned Leah)

Ashwin R.: noted. will PR runbook doc by EOD.

Jon B.: closing the thread. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
